newsitem.title: VIETNAM: U.S. trade and development chief heads for Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: U.S. trade and development chief heads for Vietnam.

text.p: Hanoi and Washington will take another step forward in their search for economic normalisation next week with a visit by the Director of the United States Trade and Development Agency (TDA) to Vietnam.
The United States Information Service in Hanoi said in a statement on Friday that Joseph Grandmaison's July 14-19 visit illustrated the TDA's wish to become a more active participant in Vietnam.

TDA helps U.S. firms contribute technology and know-how to the development of infrastructure and industrial projects in developing and middle-income countries by funding feasibility studies, orientation visits and other technical assistance.

"Mr. Grandmaison will discuss with U.S. and Vietnamese business leaders the economic development goals and objectives of the SRV (Socialist Republic of Vietnam) and specific plans to develop projects in infrastructure, transportation and related sectors of strategic importance to Vietnam," the statement said.

It said he would have meetings at the ministries of finance, industry, construction and planning and investment, Electricity of Vietnam, Petrovietnam and the Hanoi People's Committee, primarily to introduce the TDA's programmes.
Grandmaison's trip comes on the heels of a visit to Vietnam by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright last month.
While in Hanoi, Albright signed a bilateral treaty on copyright protection, which was seen as an important step towards a comprehensive trade agreement between the two former foes.
The United States has said that Vietnam must take radical steps to liberalise its trade and investment regimes for a trade agreement to be ratified.

Vietnam, which is anxious to reach an agreement because it would lead to most-favoured nation (MFN) trading status, has countered that the criteria should be less stringent because the economy is still too undeveloped.
